name: Lobuche East Peak Climbing
alt_names: Lobuche East with Everest Base Camp
sub_region: Solukhumbu District, Koshi Province (Khumbu Himal, Sagarmatha National Park, near Lobuche village)

difficulty.notes: More technical than Island Peak on the upper mountain: glacier/moraine to High Camp, then a steep snow/ice slope, an exposed south-east ridge on fixed rope, and a short near-vertical final step (operators describe about 20 m). Summit day commonly 8-12 h from High Camp with a 1-3 am start. Crampon, ice-axe, jumar and rappel skills are taught at High Camp or Base Camp. Many commercial parties stop at a false summit still some hours from the true East summit.

duration_days.basis: Full trip Kathmandu-Kathmandu, commonly combined with Everest Base Camp and Kala Patthar
duration_days.notes: Operators sell a 15-day standalone from Kathmandu (no EBC) and 18-day packages with EBC/Kala Patthar. A weather/reserve summit day is standard.

start_point: Kathmandu (fly to Lukla, or via Manthali/Ramechhap in peak seasons)

itinerary.notes: Briefing, gear check, NMA permit paperwork.

itinerary.route: Acclimatisation day: Hotel Everest View / Khumjung
Lobuche - Gorak Shep - Everest Base Camp - Gorak Shep
itinerary.notes: EBC 5,364 m. Standalone 15-day programmes skip this day and go to Base/High Camp instead.

itinerary.route: Lobuche - High Camp; rope, crampon and jumar training
itinerary.notes: Some operators overnight at Base Camp (about 5,050 m) then High Camp (listed 5,400 m or about 5,600 m).

itinerary.route: Summit Lobuche East - descend to Pheriche (or High Camp)
itinerary.notes: Rocky trail to crampon point, glacier, fixed-rope ridge, summit. Rappel on descent.

best_seasons.notes: NMA royalty is lower in autumn (USD 175) than spring (USD 350). Wind on the summit ridge is the main day-of-climb limiter in operator accounts.

permits.name: NMA climbing permit (royalty) - Lobuje East
permits.fee: USD 350 per person spring (Mar-May); USD 175 autumn (Sep-Nov), winter (Dec-Feb) and summer (Jun-Aug)
permits.valid_from: 2025-09-01 (flat per-person rate replaced old group-size tiers)

permits.name: Garbage deposit (refundable, per team)
permits.fee: USD 500 per team (NMA FAQ: all 27 NMA peaks; matches DoT schedule for peaks below 6,500 m in Khumbu)

permits.name: Sagarmatha National Park entry permit
permits.fee: NPR 3,000 per person per entry (SAARC NPR 1,500)

permits.name: Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality Trek-Card
permits.fee: NPR 3,000 per person (SAARC and Chinese nationals NPR 2,000)

guide_requirements: NMA peak permits are issued only through a registered Nepali agency, and every climbing party must be accompanied by an NMA-registered guide/sirdar (operator summaries of NMA rules; the 2025 Sixth Amendment also requires at least one mountain guide per team on peaks below 8,000 m). The trekking approach falls under the Khumbu guide-rule dispute (NTB lists Everest routes; the municipality does not enforce it).

flights: Peak-season diversion via Manthali (Ramechhap): roughly spring mid-March to May and autumn late September to end of November
drives: Kathmandu - Manthali about 4-5 h when Lukla flights are diverted
logistics.notes: Teahouses on the approach; tents at High Camp (and Base Camp if used). Fixed ropes on the upper ridge in season.

highlights: Summit of Lobuche East (6,119 m) above the Khumbu Glacier
Close views of Everest, Lhotse, Nuptse and Ama Dablam from the ridge
Everest Base Camp and Kala Patthar on the common 18-day acclimatisation trek
First recorded true-summit ascent 25 April 1984 by Larry (Laurence) Nielson and Ang Gyalzen Sherpa via the SE face/ridge (Himalayan Database; a 1979 Japanese claim is listed as disputed)
risks: Exposure and wind on the summit ridge
Fall hazard on fixed-rope rock/ice steps; rappel on descent
Stopping at the false summit (true summit is further along the ridge)

acclimatization.notes: The EBC/Kala Patthar loop adds nights near 5,000 m before High Camp. Standalone 15-day plans still use Namche and Dingboche rest days.

secondary_keywords: Lobuche East with Everest Base Camp

unverified: Summit height: NMA service-charge table and Himalayan Database give 6,119 m (used here); NMA peak list gives 6,090 m; Himalayan Database notes other map figures 6,090 m and 6,105 m.
High Camp 5,400 m vs about 5,600 m; Base Camp about 5,050 m are operator figures.
How often commercial teams continue from the false summit to the true East summit (widely reported as uncommon; no 2026 count found).
Alpine grade PD/PD+ is operator assessment, not an official NMA grade.
NMA-registered guide/sirdar requirement is from operator summaries of NMA rules, not read as a quoted NMA regulation in this research.
Some 2026 operator pages still quote the old NMA royalty (USD 250/125); the NMA table and _regulations.json are USD 350/175.
